name: Tm Visualization Suite
question: Which chart answers the question you ask of your data?
pitch: Ten chart families for Qlik Cloud, each built for a different question about time, spread, flow or parts.
useWhen: Add a chart type that a native Qlik chart does not draw.
features: See the whole spread, not just the average

hero.alt: Mosaic of six charts from the suite: a calendar heatmap, violins, a bump chart, a sunburst, a chord diagram and a mosaic.
hero.caption: Ten chart families for the questions a native Qlik chart does not answer

screenshots.alt: Correlation matrix of nine store measures, blue for positive links and red for negative links.
screenshots.caption: Compare many measures at once: which ones move together

screenshots.alt: Map of delivery locations for one region as hexagonal cells, pale in the dense centre and darker toward the edges.
screenshots.caption: Put locations on a map and see where they cluster

screenshots.alt: Calendar heatmap of daily sales over three years, one block per year, with the darkest days around December.
screenshots.caption: Every day of three years in one view

questions: Which chart fits my question about time, spread or flow?
How do I show a process, a hierarchy or a map in Qlik?
Can one set of charts cover my whole analytics team?
audience: Analysts and BI leads who build Qlik sheets and need charts that a native Qlik chart does not draw.

featureStrips.heading: Follow time and the seasons
featureStrips.text: Calendar heatmaps, ridgelines and streamgraphs show the rhythm of your numbers over days, weeks and years.
featureStrips.alt: Streamgraph of monthly sales by product group, stacked areas that widen and narrow over time.

featureStrips.heading: See the whole spread, not just the average
featureStrips.text: Violins, rainclouds and beeswarms show how values spread inside and between groups.
featureStrips.alt: Raincloud chart for four delivery methods with points on the left and a half violin and box on the right.

featureStrips.heading: Compare categories, ranges and ranks
featureStrips.text: Dumbbells, dot plots and bump charts show who changed, by how much and who overtook whom.
featureStrips.alt: Vertical dumbbell chart of net sales for two fiscal years per store, grouped by store format.

featureStrips.heading: Follow flows and links
featureStrips.text: Chords, alluvial diagrams and networks show who connects to whom, and how strong the link is.
featureStrips.alt: Alluvial diagram with suppliers on the left and receiving sites on the right, joined by bands of different widths.

featureStrips.heading: Break a total into levels
featureStrips.text: Sunbursts, icicles and trees show how a total splits into categories and sub-categories.
featureStrips.alt: Icicle chart of net sales by product group and sub-category, with one colour per group.

featureStrips.heading: Walk through a process
featureStrips.text: Traces, swimlanes and journeys show how cases move through steps, and where they wait.
featureStrips.alt: Swimlane chart of order events grouped by team: customer, payment, store, customer service and carrier.

featureStrips.heading: Show the parts of a whole
featureStrips.text: Waffles, unit charts and mosaics show how a total splits into parts, and how the mix differs by group.
featureStrips.alt: Unit chart with one symbol per order for four delivery methods, coloured by order channel.

featureStrips.heading: Check actual against plan and target
featureStrips.text: Bullets, waterfalls and pace charts show who is ahead of plan, who is behind and by how much.
featureStrips.alt: Waterfall chart from an opening value of 605 to a closing value of 620 with increases and decreases per item.
